claims.scope: limit order book doubly-linked list maintenance: appending a new order to an existing limit and removing a middle order

preconditions.text: A new order is appended to an existing limit via _updateLimitPostOrder.; At that point the order lives only in memory.; The newly added order ends up with a zero prevOrderId.; The list contains order3 (tail) linked to order2 linked to order1 (head).; A middle order (order2) of the list is removed (canceled/amended/filled).
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.

safety.text: Removing a middle order from a correctly doubly-linked limit list should preserve the remaining orders' prev/next links so that the head order stays reachable and fillable.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.

effects.text: After removing order2, order1 is lost track of and becomes unfillable.
effects.derivation: Program-generated direct negation witness for the selected safety pattern.

effect_coverage.reason: Program-generated exact coverage for selected direct impact.

assumptions: The removal is triggered by cancel/amend/fill of a middle order in a list that was correctly doubly-linked before the append.
The append flow adds a new order to an existing limit while the order lives only in memory.
The prevOrderId reference used during removal is the zero value caused by the missing storage write-back.

limitations: Concrete order ids, list contents, and storage layout are symbolic placeholders; only the reported structural relation is encoded.
The prev_list_broken effect is a general list-integrity consequence and is deferred as a secondary consequence of the same trigger.
The security intent's fillability reachability is captured through the head_order_lost effect; no separate numeric economic loss is modeled.
The inferred else-branch mechanism is treated as context, not as a selected precondition predicate.
